message.content:
Let \(p=2027\) and \(N=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). Work modulo \(p\).

For \(k>N\), we have \(p \le 2k < 2p\), so \(p\mid (2k)!\) but \(p\nmid k!\). Hence
\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv 0 \pmod p,
\]
so only \(0\le k\le N\) contribute.

We claim that for \(0\le k\le N\),
\[
\binom{2k}{k}2^k \equiv \binom{N}{k}(-8)^k \pmod p.
\]
Indeed,
\[
\binom{N}{k}(-4)^k
=\frac{1}{k!}\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(-4)(N-j).
\]
Since \(N=(p-1)/2\),
\[
-4(N-j)=-4N+4j=2+4j\equiv 2(2j+1)\pmod p.
\]
Thus
\[
\binom{N}{k}(-4)^k
\equiv \frac{1}{k!}\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}2(2j+1)
=\frac{(2k)!}{(k!)^2}
=\binom{2k}{k}.
\]
Multiplying by \(2^k\) gives the claim.

Therefore the polynomial
\[
A(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\binom{2k}{k}2^k x^k
\]
satisfies
\[
A(x)\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{N}\binom{N}{k}(-8x)^k=(1-8x)^N \pmod p.
\]
So
\[
S=A'(1)\equiv -8N(1-8)^{N-1}\pmod p.
\]
With \(N=1013\),
\[
-8N=-4(p-1)\equiv 4,\qquad 1-8\equiv -7,
\]
hence
\[
S\equiv 4(-7)^{1012}=4\cdot 7^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

By Euler’s criterion,
\[
7^{1013}\equiv \left(\frac{7}{2027}\right).
\]
By quadratic reciprocity,
\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
=\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)(-1)^{3\cdot1013}
=\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)(-1)=-1.
\]
Thus
\[
7^{1012}\equiv -7^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]
Since \(7\cdot1448=10136=5\cdot2027+1\), we have \(7^{-1}\equiv1448\), so
\[
7^{1012}\equiv -1448\equiv 579\pmod{2027}.
\]
Finally,
\[
S\equiv 4\cdot579=2316\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
